previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted due to gangrene and infection of the right fourth toe. He underwent amputation, and tissue cultures confirmed E. coli and anaerobic bacteria. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics, initially vancomycin and Zosyn, then transitioned to outpatient ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for a six-week course. His blood pressure was elevated during admission, prompting an increase in spironolactone dose. Kidney function remained stable within his baseline, and he was discharged home in stable condition with plans for wound follow-up, infectious disease management, and weekly lab monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Uncontrolled DM2 status post renal transplant on immunosuppressives.
Here with fevers, prior right toe amputation, now ulcer near distal end of
first metatarsal.  Question osteomyelitis, evidence of infection.

RIGHT FOOT, THREE VIEWS:

COMPARISON:  Right foot radiographs dated ___.

As before, there is evidence of amputation of the first toe.  The edge of the
distal first metatarsal appears relatively well corticated and no superimposed
osteolysis is identified.  However, compared with the prior film, there is new
osteolysis involving the previously seen right fourth proximal phalanx bony
remnant with an overlying lucency suggestive of ulceration.  The proximal
phalangeal remnants of the second and third toes and of the fifth toe are
grossly unchanged ,without aggressive osteolysis.  Vascular calcification
noted.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No definite interval change involving the distal first metatarsal.
2.  Interval osteolysis of the previously seen fourth proximal phalanx
remnant.  In the appropriate clinical setting, this is highly suggestive of
osteomyelitis.
